candidates.title: Care and longevity demand are becoming an access-time-work capacity problem
candidates.mechanism: Aging, health needs, and care demand create pressure through waiting time, unpaid care, employment tradeoffs, household room, and uneven service capacity.
candidates.counter_signal: Company examples include discretionary pet-wellness offers, while care-access records span different countries, populations, periods, and institutional systems.
candidates.next_test: Build a comparable dated panel of care demand, access/waiting time, unpaid-care hours, employment effect, service capacity, and spending across independent source families.

candidates.title: Adaptation demand is shifting toward control, proof, substitution, and resilience
candidates.mechanism: Under instability, buyers may pay for workflow control, compliance proof, trusted guidance, substitution, and resilience rather than novelty alone.
candidates.counter_signal: The inputs are synthesis layers and a source-linked company coverage measure; they do not establish population demand or willingness to pay.
candidates.next_test: Compare dated spending, procurement, adoption, retention, compliance cost, switching, and outcome measures across independent source families for the same mechanism and geography.
